newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares end firmer, bucking global trend.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares end firmer, bucking global trend.

text.p: Belgian shares ended flat to firm on Monday, bucking the trend on most markets, with dealers attributing the performance to portfolio managers.

Buying in selected blue chips left the Bel-20 index up 7.53 points, or 0.32 percent, at 2,380.70 points at the close. Other markets were negative after U.S. data released late in the day re-kindled fears the July 1-2 meeting of the U.S. Fed's rate-setting committee would decide to raise rates.
One trader suggested the selective buying was half-year window-dressing by fund managers. Another said however it was portfolios being adjusted for the launch of a new FT index.
"In the last 10-years I have never heard of window-dressing on June 30," he said. "We had some unusual volumes today but I think it was people preparing for a new FT index."
In July the Financial Times plans to launch the Eurotop 300 index of Europe's biggest capitalised companies. A Europe 100 index will also be launched.
Belgium's top 15 companies in terms of market capitalisation will be in the Eurotop 300.
A late rise in insurance company Fortis AG stood out among a number of unusual price and volume movements, ending the day up 3.19 percent at 7,430 francs -- an all-time high.
"I think it's been manipulated a bit," one trader said. "That is a price set for 59 shares. The price before was 7,400 francs and the bid/offer spread was 7,370/80 francs."
He said electronics group Barco had also risen unusually quickly, adding nearly three percent to 7,290 francs.

A 2.59 percent gain in shares in non-ferrous metals maker Union Miniere was attributed to the sharp overnight rise in the dollar, which automatically boosts the company's bottom line, and firm zinc prices.
Another unsual mover was holding company CNP/NPM, whose share gained 40 francs to 2,760 in volume of 63,094 shares, about 10 times more than average.
CNP has consistently said it is undervalued and has recently started publishing its net asset value in newspapers.
One trader suggested that CNP might be exercising its policy of buying shares when it believed the discount was too great.
Shares in blue chip holding company GBL, a key CNP asset, ended down 60 francs at 6,030.
